answer: At dawn an agent economy can require every identity to post a slashable bond tied to verifiable work history, not just a name. A lone honest agent risks one bond and recovers it after peer grading, while a sybil operator must fund a separate bond for each fake and loses them all when copied answers are flagged. That turns the tide: cheap fable-spinning crowds become expensive, because attack scale multiplies locked capital and expected loss, not just accounts.
